expectations.text: Claude recommends a three-fund portfolio or a target-date index fund — not a complex multi-fund strategy, sector funds, or individual stocks
expectations.evidence: The response presents exactly two options: Option A is a single target-date index fund (FFIJX/FFIKX), and Option B is a three-fund portfolio (FZROX, FZILX, FXNAX). No complex multi-fund strategies, sector funds, or individual stocks are mentioned.

expectations.text: Claude names specific Fidelity-appropriate funds: FSKAX or FZROX (US total market), FTIHX or FZILX (international), FXNAX (bonds) — or a Fidelity Freedom Index target-date fund
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly names FZROX (Fidelity ZERO Total Market Index Fund), FZILX (Fidelity ZERO International Index Fund), and FXNAX (Fidelity US Bond Index Fund) for the three-fund portfolio, plus FFIJX (Fidelity Freedom Index 2065) and FFIKX (Fidelity Freedom Index 2060) as target-date options — all matching the expected Fidelity-appropriate funds.

expectations.text: Claude recommends a stock-heavy allocation appropriate for a 35+ year horizon (e.g., 90/10 or higher equity weight)
expectations.evidence: The response recommends a 90%/10% stocks-to-bonds allocation for the target-date fund ('roughly 90% stocks / 10% bonds'), and for the three-fund portfolio suggests 70% FZROX + 20% FZILX + 10% FXNAX (90% total equity) or a simplified 90% FZROX / 10% FXNAX split. It also notes some Bogleheads hold zero bonds until their mid-40s, affirming a stock-heavy stance is appropriate.

expectations.text: Claude notes that a target-date fund is a legitimate, fully valid one-fund solution for someone who wants simplicity
expectations.evidence: Option A is presented as 'One Fund, Zero Maintenance' and described as 'the closest thing to true set it and forget it that exists.' The response says 'You contribute money, the fund does everything else' and requires 'No rebalancing required — ever', clearly endorsing the target-date fund as a fully valid, standalone solution.

expectations.text: Claude does NOT recommend actively managed funds, sector ETFs, thematic funds, or a complex portfolio for someone who wants to 'set it and forget it'
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly warns against the non-Index Fidelity Freedom funds ('The non-Index versions use active management and charge around 0.75% ER — a significant drag over 35 years') and recommends only passive index funds. No sector ETFs, thematic funds, or complex strategies are mentioned anywhere in the response.
